question: A man drives his car at a speed of 50 km / hr for 2 hours and then decides to slow down to 40 km / hr till the end of the journey. If his average speed for the journey was 44 km / hr, then for how much time he drives his car at speed 40 km / hr?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By applying the rule of alligation on speeds, we can directly find the ratio of the time taken.

Ratio of Time = (Average Speed − Speed 2) : (Speed 1 − Average Speed)

Time Ratio = (44 − 40) : (50 − 44) = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3

The time taken at 50 km/hr is given as 2 hours, which perfectly matches the 2 ratio parts.

Thus, the time taken at 40 km/hr exactly equals the 3 ratio parts.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**
